name: Normteile Brucker KG
summary: Normteile Brucker KG is a family-owned standard-parts maker founded in 1966, with 60 staff, EUR 29.1 M turnover and stable, sound finances. It runs a strict list-price policy: head office has frozen all price reductions until December 2027, the price list applies to all customers, and changes above 2 % go to a pricing committee that meets every two weeks. It openly invites talks on payment, logistics and call-off flexibility instead of price.

situation.decision_maker: Key account manager up to 2 %; above 2 % the pricing committee (meets every two weeks); head office has frozen price reductions until Dec 2027.

negotiation_pattern: On part:360013 (stud bolt) it offered small cuts itself and settled lower each year: asked -5.1 % and settled -6.3 %, asked -1.1 % and settled -2.8 %, asked -0.7 % and settled -3.8 %. On part:360030 (washer) it asked +1.7 %, +3.5 % and +1.2 % and always settled at 0 %. So it accepts zero instead of fighting for increases and gives about 2 % more than its opening. Since 2026 it has hardened. It cites a head-office freeze, re-quoted 360013 unchanged on 2026-09-04, and steers talks to payment and logistics. It said only multi-year volume agreements change prices.
wants: payment discipline and better payment conditions (it offered to discuss them; we pay late on 90 % of invoices)
multi-year volume security (its stated only route to price changes)
a larger quota on part:360030 (currently 50 %, one alternative source)
call-off and logistics efficiency (returnable boxes, flexible call-offs)
protects: unit_price (list-price policy, reductions frozen until Dec 2027, applies to all customers)
any price move above 2 % (needs pricing committee)

trades.give: payment discipline: pay on time at 30 days net, or faster payment (e.g. 10–14 days)
trades.get: skonto (e.g. 2 % for 14 days) as a price-neutral discount instead of a list-price cut
trades.why: It openly offers to discuss payment terms; a skonto leaves its list price untouched.

trades.give: contract_months: extend the framework beyond 2027-06-30 to a multi-year term, plus volume_per_year: move part:360030 from 50 % to 100 % quota
trades.get: unit_price -2 % on both parts from 2027-01-01 (within account-manager authority, no committee)
trades.why: It said only multi-year volume agreements change prices, and 2 % stays below its committee threshold.

trades.give: call-off flexibility and a rolling forecast
trades.get: lead_time_days held at 7 with an OTD commitment toward the 95 % target, plus prices fixed through 2027 with no index_clause
trades.why: It is open on call-off flexibility; its OTD of 88 % is below the contract target.

trades.give: the larger quota and longer term from the second trade
trades.get: ppm_commitment ≤200, closure of the open 8D, and chargeback_eur_per_complaint kept at 150 or raised
trades.why: ppm rose from 216 to 257 (peak 293) over the year; quality terms cost it no list price.

arguments.point: You told us only multi-year volume agreements change prices. Here is one: a longer term plus 100 % of the washer volume.
We keep the request at 2 %, so your key account manager can approve it without waiting for the pricing committee.
You invited a discussion on payment conditions. We commit to on-time or faster payment in exchange for skonto.
OTD of 88 % is well below the 95 % contract target, and ppm has risen over the year. We expect a firm delivery and quality commitment in return for more volume.
In past renewals you settled below your opening on the stud bolt and held the washer at 0 %. We ask for the same constructive approach.

avoid: Demanding a straight list-price cut without a counter-offer; it will cite the head-office freeze and stall.
Asking for more than 2 % in one step; that triggers the biweekly pricing committee and delays.
Threatening to move volume; we are only 0.3 % of its turnover, so the threat carries little weight.
Pressing on payment terms while we pay late on 90 % of invoices; fix our own discipline first.
Treating it as a cost-plus case; no should-cost data exists.
tone: Factual, respectful and structured. Package each ask as a term-for-term trade, keep price asks within 2 %, and acknowledge its policy.
red_flags: part:360013 is single-sourced (100 % quota, 0 other sources); it is a standard part, but requalifying takes time.
OTD is 88 % against a 95 % target and has been flat to falling for four quarters.
ppm is rising (216 → 257, peak 293), 19 complaints in 12 months, 1 open 8D, last complaint 2026-09-09.
We pay late on 90 % of invoices (mean 4.4 days after due), which weakens our position and the relationship.
Price-change notice under the contract is 90 days before year end, so the window for 2027 effectively closes around 2026-10-02.
It cites a 'head office' although no group parent is recorded; treat it as internal family management policy, not a group rule.

evidence.claim: Head office froze all price reductions until December 2027; the sales director was open on payment terms and call-off flexibility.
The price list applies to all customers without exception until December 2027; it is happy to discuss logistics and payment conditions.
Price changes above 2 % need pricing committee approval; the committee meets every two weeks.
Only multi-year volume agreements change prices on standard items.
The latest quote re-offers part:360013 at the current 29.23/100 with 'no discounts this year (head-office directive)'.
Finances are stable: credit index 185, unchanged from 12 months ago, and equity ratio 36.2 %.
OTD is 88 % against the 95 % contract target, with ppm at 257 in 2026Q3.
Historically it settled about 2 % below its opening; washer increase asks always ended at 0 %.
The framework runs to 2027-06-30 and auto-extends 12 months; prices are fixed per calendar year with 90 days' notice.

indicators.credit_index: 185 (12 months ago 185; higher is worse, >300 weak)
indicators.scorecard_trend: 2025Q4 green (otd 89.6, ppm 216) → 2026Q1 green (otd 89.6, ppm 270) → 2026Q2 green (otd 88.0, ppm 293) → 2026Q3 green (otd 88.0, ppm 257)
